metadata.name: Cockcroft-Gault Creatinine Clearance (CrCl)
metadata.summary: Estimates creatinine clearance (mL/min) for renal dose adjustments of DOACs, antiepileptics (levetiracetam, gabapentin, pregabalin), and antimicrobials.
clinical_pearls: FDA drug labels and pivotal DOAC trials (RE-LY, ROCKET AF, ARISTOTLE, ENGAGE AF) specify Cockcroft-Gault CrCl rather than eGFR for renal dosing cutoffs.
In obese patients (> 120% ideal body weight), consider using Ideal Body Weight (IBW) or Adjusted Body Weight (AdjBW) to avoid overestimating CrCl (Winter et al., 2012; Brown et al., 2013).
Outputs unindexed CrCl in mL/min (incorporating body weight), unlike BSA-indexed MDRD or CKD-EPI eGFR (mL/min/1.73 m²).

Pitfall — Overestimation & assay drift: CrCl typically overestimates true GFR due to tubular creatinine secretion; additionally, the 1976 equation was derived from non-IDMS-standardized creatinine in a predominantly male (96%) cohort.

items.label: Body Weight
items.subtitle: Actual body weight (or IBW/AdjBW in obesity)

interpretation.label: Kidney Failure (CrCl < 15 mL/min)
interpretation.summary: Severe renal failure; most renally cleared neuro-medications and DOACs are contraindicated or require dialysis-specific dosing.

interpretation.label: Severe Reduction (15–29.9 mL/min)
interpretation.summary: Markedly reduced clearance; dabigatran is contraindicated for AF (< 30 mL/min) and rivaroxaban/apixaban/levetiracetam require major dose reduction.

interpretation.label: Moderate Reduction (30–59.9 mL/min)
interpretation.summary: Renal dose adjustments often required (e.g., rivaroxaban 15 mg OD for AF if CrCl 15–49; levetiracetam/gabapentin/pregabalin/acyclovir adjustments).

interpretation.label: Mildly Decreased (60–89.9 mL/min)
interpretation.summary: Mildly decreased creatinine clearance; standard dosing applies for most agents except narrow-therapeutic-index drugs.

interpretation.label: Normal / Preserved (>= 90 mL/min)
interpretation.summary: Preserved renal clearance; monitor for augmented renal clearance in young neurocritical care trauma/SAH patients.

assessment_guides.title: Actual vs Ideal vs Adjusted Body Weight
bedside_steps: If actual body weight (ABW) < ideal body weight (IBW), use ABW.
If ABW is between 100% and 120% of IBW, use IBW or ABW per institutional protocol.
If ABW > 120% of IBW (obesity), use Adjusted Body Weight: AdjBW = IBW + 0.4 * (ABW - IBW).
pitfalls_and_exceptions: Cockcroft-Gault is invalid in acute kidney injury (rapidly changing creatinine) or severe sarcopenia/cachexia.

references.citation: Cockcroft DW, Gault MH. Prediction of creatinine clearance from serum creatinine. Nephron. 1976;16(1):31-41.
Winter MA, Guhr KN, Berg GM. Impact of various body weights and serum creatinine concentrations on the bias and accuracy of the Cockcroft-Gault equation. Pharmacotherapy. 2012;32(7):604-612.

Brown DL, Masselink AJ, Lalla CD. Functional range of creatinine clearance for renal drug dosing: a practical solution to the controversy of which weight to use in the Cockcroft-Gault equation. Ann Pharmacother. 2013;47(7-8):1039-1044.
